methods.label: Read the scales and use similarity
methods.explanation:
The numbered scales place \(A\) at 3 and \(B\) at 4, while their associated endpoints \(A'\) and \(B'\) are at 5 and 1. Thus the association reverses direction and maps an interval of length 1 onto an interval of length 4.

Let \(O\) be the common intersection of the three connecting lines. The parallel scales give equal corresponding angles, so \(\triangle OAB\) and \(\triangle OA'B'\) are similar, with length ratio \(4:1\). Applying the same angle argument to the triangles with bases \(AP\) and \(A'P'\) gives
\[
A'P'=4AP.
\]
This also holds at \(P=A\), where both lengths are zero.

When \(x=a\), we have \(3\le a\le4\) and \(AP=a-3\). Since \(A'\) is at reading 5 and \(P'\) lies toward the smaller readings,
\[
y=5-A'P'=5-4(a-3).
\]
Consequently,
\[
x+y=a+5-4(a-3)=\boxed{17-3a}.
\]
The endpoints give \((x,y)=(3,5)\) and \((4,1)\), as depicted. The answer is \(\text{C}\).
